B4a-04-tadpole-external-internal-gills

Two stages of a tadpole in side view. Left: a young tadpole with three pairs of feathery external gills (bright red) sticking out on each side behind the head. Right: an older tadpole with the gills covered by skin, and a small opening (the spiracle) on the left side, with arrows showing water entering the mouth and leaving through the spiracle. Draw only the outside of the tadpoles, as solid opaque bodies. Do not show any internal organs, no cutaway, no see-through body.
B4a-01-respiratory-surface-exchange

A simple close-up diagram of a generalised respiratory surface: a thin moist layer of cells one cell thick between the outside (air or water) on the left and a blood capillary with red blood cells on the right. Arrows show oxygen diffusing from the outside into the blood and carbon dioxide diffusing from the blood to the outside. A thin film of moisture lines the outer surface.
B4a-03-fish-gill-structure-countercurrent

Two parts. Left: the head of a Tilapia fish in side view with the operculum cut away to reveal four curved gills, with an arrow showing water entering the mouth and leaving under the operculum. Right: an enlarged single gill showing the curved bony gill arch, short pale gill rakers on its inner side, two rows of bright red gill filaments on its outer side, and an inset of one filament with thin lamellae and capillaries, with arrows showing water flowing one way and blood flowing the opposite way.
B4a-05-cockroach-tracheal-system-anatomy

Top view (dorsal view) of a cockroach outline showing the tracheal system in silver-white: ten pairs of spiracles along the sides (two on the thorax, eight on the abdomen), each leading to short tracheae that join two main longitudinal tracheal trunks along each side, with branches to the legs, head and organs. An inset shows an enlarged trachea with spiral chitin thickening branching into very fine tracheoles ending among muscle cells, with a little fluid at the tracheole ends. Another inset shows a spiracle with hairs and a valve.
B4a-06-human-respiratory-system-anatomy

Front view of the human respiratory system: head in side profile showing the nasal cavity, pharynx, epiglottis and larynx, then the trachea with visible C-shaped cartilage rings running down into the chest, dividing into two bronchi and branching bronchioles inside two lungs (one lung drawn cut open to show branching). The ribs (shown in section), intercostal muscles and dome-shaped diaphragm below the lungs, and the pleural membranes around the lungs. An inset shows a cluster of alveoli at the end of a bronchiole, wrapped in red and blue capillaries.
B4a-08-leaf-epidermis-stomata-structure

Surface view of a piece of lower leaf epidermis showing irregular, jigsaw-shaped epidermal cells without chloroplasts and several stomata, each between two kidney-shaped guard cells containing green chloroplasts; one stoma drawn open and one closed. Beside it, a small vertical section through a stoma showing the guard cells, the pore and the substomatal air space leading into the spongy mesophyll. A small inset shows dumbbell-shaped guard cells of a grass.
B4a-09-lenticels-mangrove-pneumatophores

Two panels. Left: a young woody twig with small raised pale lenticels dotted on its brown bark, and an enlarged vertical section through one lenticel showing tightly packed brown cork cells on either side, a mass of loosely packed round cells with air spaces pushing up through a split in the bark, the cork cambium below, and arrows showing oxygen entering and carbon dioxide leaving. Right: mangrove pneumatophores sticking up from grey waterlogged mud, with lenticels on them.
B4a-13-bell-jar-lung-model

The bell jar model of the lungs in two states side by side. Each shows a bell jar with a rubber stopper and Y-shaped glass tube at the top, two balloons on the arms of the tube inside, and a rubber sheet tied across the bottom with a small knob. Left: rubber sheet pulled down, balloons inflated, arrow showing air entering the tube. Right: rubber sheet pushed up, balloons deflated, arrow showing air leaving.
B4a-10-stoma-opening-closing-mechanism

Two side-by-side surface views of a pair of kidney-shaped guard cells. Left (stoma open, in light): swollen turgid guard cells curved apart, with blue arrows showing water entering, small orange dots representing potassium ions inside, and a small sun symbol. Right (stoma closed, in dark): thin, flaccid, straight guard cells pressed together, with arrows showing water and potassium ions leaving, and a small moon symbol. The thick inner walls are drawn darker than the outer walls in both.
B4a-11-fish-ventilation-mechanism-stages

Two-step diagram of breathing in a bony fish, each step shown as a simple horizontal section through the head seen from above. Step 1 (inspiration): mouth open, floor of buccal cavity lowered (shown by a downward arrow), operculum closed, water arrows entering the mouth. Step 2 (expiration): mouth closed, floor of buccal cavity raised (upward arrow), water arrows passing over the gills and out under the open operculum.
B4a-12-human-breathing-mechanism-ventilation

Two side-by-side front views of the human chest showing the rib cage, lungs and diaphragm. Left (inspiration): ribs raised and moved outwards (arrows up and out), diaphragm flattened (arrow down), lungs larger, arrow showing air entering the trachea. Right (expiration): ribs lowered (arrows down and in), diaphragm domed upwards (arrow up), lungs smaller, arrow showing air leaving. A small side-view inset in each shows the sternum moving up and forward in inspiration and down and back in expiration.
B4a-02-amoeba-earthworm-respiration

Two panels. Left: an Amoeba in pond water, with small arrows all round its outline showing oxygen diffusing in and carbon dioxide diffusing out across the cell membrane. Right: an earthworm on damp soil with a cut-away block of its body wall showing the thin cuticle, epidermis with mucus gland cells, and a dense network of red capillaries just under the surface, with arrows showing oxygen entering from the air and carbon dioxide leaving.
B4a-14-alveolus-gas-exchange-capillary

Close-up of a single alveolus in section with a capillary wrapped against its wall. The alveolus wall and capillary wall are each one cell thick, with a thin film of moisture lining the alveolus. Blue (deoxygenated) blood enters the capillary from one side and leaves as red (oxygenated) blood on the other. Arrows show oxygen diffusing from the alveolar air into a red blood cell and carbon dioxide diffusing from the plasma into the alveolus.
